answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, so a sybil set’s influence depends on paths entering from trusted nodes. If its volume-normalized cut has conductance φ, the probability a stationary walk exits within t steps is at most tφ; thus a sparse external cut limits reachable voting weight. Min-cut transitivity bounds prevent mirror, umber, or tundra clusters from amplifying internal attestations into broad trust.
